xmldoc.short_description: Run an external program and stream its standard input and output.

param_input_item.param_description: string scalar or character vector: the program to start.
string scalars or character vectors: command-line arguments passed to the program.

description.p: nelson.os.Process starts an external program and returns an object that streams its standard input and output without blocking the interpreter.
The program runs in the background. Its output is buffered as it arrives and is read on demand; input is written to the program at any time.

A real program is launched directly on every platform, with no shell: on Windows the command is resolved against the PATH and PATHEXT (a .bat or .cmd script is run through the command shell automatically).
This feature is not available in the WebAssembly build.
Properties (read with dot notation, for example p.Running):
Command: the program that was started.
Arguments: the command-line arguments, as a cell array.
WorkingDirectory: the working directory of the program.
ProcessId: the operating-system process identifier.
Running: true while the program is still running.
ExitCode: the exit code once the program has finished, otherwise empty.
BytesAvailable: the number of output bytes buffered and ready to read.
Methods (called with dot notation, for example p.read()):
write(data): send bytes to the program standard input, from a character vector, string scalar, or uint8 vector.
read(): read and return all buffered standard output as a character vector.
readline(): read and return the next complete output line, or an empty character vector when no line is ready.
stderr(): read and return all buffered standard error as a character vector.
close(): close the standard input, signalling end of input to the program.
wait(timeout): block until the program exits or the timeout in seconds elapses; a negative or omitted timeout waits forever.
terminate(): stop the program and its child processes.
Use delete(p) to terminate the program and release the object.

example_item.example_item_description: Start a program, read its output, then release the object.
